denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Osteoarthritis of knee was first diagnosed on 2026-05-10, AFTER the policy start date 2024-02-27; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period – Claim ID 26607f6f-ade3-4356-a76d-fb1961b99dd0  

Claim Details:  
- Claim ID: 26607f6f-ade3-4356-a76d-fb1961b99dd0  
- Patient ID: 3893951a-b978-4bd4-bcf1-021e390f0764  
- Patient Name: Rahul Sharma  
- Date of Service: 2026‑05‑10  
- Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER)  
- Coverage Start Date: 2024‑02‑27  
- Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (first diagnosed on 2026‑05‑10)  
- Procedure: Physical therapy procedure  
- Claim Amount: INR 24,747.95  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The insurer’s denial relies on the premise that the claim is subject to the Pre‑Existing Disease (PED) waiting period. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is expressly excluded from the PED definition and therefore the waiting period does not apply [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Osteoarthritis of the knee for Mr. Sharma was first diagnosed on 2026‑05‑10, which is after the policy commencement on 2024‑02‑27, satisfying the “on or after” criterion. Consequently, the PED waiting period in Clause 4.2 is inapplicable to this claim [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating orthopaedic specialist will attach detailed clinical notes confirming that the prescribed physical therapy is medically necessary for the management of Mr. Sharma’s newly diagnosed osteoarthritis of the knee.  

Reference to Denial Standards:  
The denial does not identify the specific policy clause applied to the facts, contrary to the requirement for a reasoned denial [claims_procedure_and_grievance#5]. Moreover, the burden of proof for applying a waiting‑period exclusion rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date. No such evidence has been supplied; therefore the insurer has not met its evidentiary burden [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the above, we request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 24,747.95 be paid in full to the provider.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.1 Reasoned Denial
citations.quote:
## C3. Standards for Denial  
### C3.1 Reasoned Denial
Every denial must state the specific policy clause relied upon and the facts that bring the claim within that clause. A denial that does not identify the clause, or that applies a clause to facts outside its definition, is not a valid denial.
